title: Forming his own quintet in New York with Jimmy Forrest
summary: At Teddy Reig's urging he formed a Birdland group with Forrest, Joe Benjamin, Jimmy Jones, later Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, why did you decide to go back to New York at this point?

Well, Teddy had been calling me, Teddy Reig. And he said, well, we want you to go in the Birdland. And you get your own group together. Naturally, every musician wants to experience having his own band, you know.
Oh, yes, you almost wanted to --

Yeah, wanted to go to New York, anyway. So I think my first was Jimmy Forrest, Joe Benjamin and Jimmy Jones was on piano, and oh, what's the drummer's name in New York, not Elvin because Elvin came latter. He played with Billy Eckstine for a long time. Good drummer.* Anyway, they opened up with me. And it was a fantastic night, you know.
And Joe Benjamin, after he left, then I got Tommy Potter and Tommy Flanagan and Elvin Jones.
Oh, you had Elvin in that band?
Well, how was he coming in?
That's what I figured because you wouldn't have stood for --
Oh, no. He was an all together different drummer. He was an all together different drummer then. He was main swing. And Elvin still can swing.
Yes, I know. But later he got into/terribly loud, you know. that...
Well, it became fashionable for drummers to play like that. And we went on tour. I had a good band. I had a really good band.
